Issued at 300 PM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Today-Tonight... High pressure holds influence over much of the 
eastern U.S. today. Increasing northeast winds are observed on the 
south side of the high pressure this afternoon with may areas of 
central Florida seeing peak gusts exceeding 20-25 mph so far 
today. A Wind Advisory is currently in effect for portions of the 
coast including Volusia and northern Brevard, before extending 
southward through the remainder of the coast this evening as wind 
gusts increase to 35 mph. Onshore moving showers have been ongoing
through much of the morning and have shown an increase in 
coverage north of the Cape and the Orlando Metro early this 
afternoon. Rounds of scattered to numerous quick moving showers 
are forecast to continue through the evening and overnight, and 
coastal areas which see repeated rounds of heavy rainfall may 
become vulnerable to ponding of water or minor flooding. Despite 
cold temperatures aloft (500mb), poor lapse rates between the 
700-500mb layer have largely limited lightning and storm 
potential, and lightning chances remain low through the remainder 
of today and into tonight. Low temperatures fall to range the 
upper 60s across much of east central Florida early Sunday morning
while areas near the coast may hold closer to 70 degrees. 

Sunday-Tuesday... A tightening pressure gradient is expected into 
Sunday as high pressure persists over the eastern U.S. and low 
pressure begins to gradually organize over the western Atlantic. 
Gusty northeast winds strengthen on Sunday, persisting into the 
workweek. A Wind Advisory continues along the coast Sunday, but most 
ensemble probabilities do not show enough confidence to expand inland 
at this time. Therefore, expect wind gusts of 30-35 mph along the 
coast, remaining closer to 30 mph inland on Sunday with gusty 
conditions persisting Monday and Tuesday. The long duration onshore 
wind event will continue hazardous to dangerous beach and marine 
conditions. A high risk of life-threatening rip currents and rough 
surf is expected with large breaking waves of 7-11 ft, and a High 
Surf Advisory continues at least through Monday. Entering the water 
is strongly discouraged! Long period swells exceeding 10-12 seconds 
combined with pounding surf will contribute to Moderate to Major 
beach erosion at area beaches. Wind driven coastal impacts will be 
further enhanced by a period of astronomical high tides. Wave runup 
during the morning high tide cycles will result in Minor to Moderate 
coastal flooding, especially Monday and Tuesday mornings, and a 
Coastal Flood Warning in effect Sunday and Monday will likely need 
to be extended into Tuesday. Heading to the beach could become 
hazardous, especially during times of high tide.

Passing pockets of locally higher moisture will support rounds of 
onshore moving showers on Sunday. Greatest rain chances are forecast 
in vicinity of the coastal I-95 corridor (50-80%) while scattered 
(20-40%) rounds of showers should still manage to push inland. 
Lightning chances remain low. However, showers will be capable of 
localized gusty winds 40-45 mph and heavy downpours. General 
consensus among deterministic and ensemble model suites has 
highlighted an area of higher QPF across portions of southeast 
Florida on Sunday, extending northward through portions of the 
Treasure Coast counties. A slight risk for excessive rainfall exists 
for these areas, and cannot rule out ponding water or minor flooding 
where multiple rounds of heavy rainfall occurs. Rounds of showers 
remain forecast Sunday night before a drier airmass begins to advect 
southward. This will reduce interior rain chances Monday and 
Tuesday. Scattered rain chances persist along the coast Monday, 
becoming limited south of the Cape by Tuesday. 

High temperatures remain seasonal early next week, mostly in the low 
80s. Low temperatures in the mid to upper 60s across the interior 
will be a few degrees warmer across the coastal counties each day. 

Wednesday-Friday (previous)...Discrepancies persist in guidance 
relative to the strength of the pressure gradient mid to late week, 
primarily driven by differing placement and strength of the 
lingering low pressure system out in the Atlantic. These should 
resolve over time after the low develops. Regardless, breezy and 
gusty northeast winds are anticipated to persist across east central 
Florida, resulting in prolonged hazardous coastal and surf 
conditions. Additionally, this flow will support development of 
onshore-moving showers and isolated storms, with the highest chances 
focused along the coast. Lower chances across the interior, though 
it cannot be fully ruled out. Temperatures are forecast to remain 
near normal values for this time of year.
